ticket: PL-12 — /inline-edit: a sanctioned, spec-first front door for a direct in-session edit
goal: Give a direct, in-session edit — no prior pipeline run, no production incident — a sanctioned front door: /inline-edit, a lane that mechanically refuses to let any code change happen before a real, ratified spec.md/spec.json exists for it, then runs tester -> review -> security in full against the edited tree, states at every stop exactly what is still owed for the record, and ends in a ledger entry that is visibly and structurally distinct from a full run — one that says plainly that the implementation was a direct inline edit and that red never ran. Today that path is either an unrecorded hand-edit (the D-005 #3 failure) or a disproportionate full /pipeline run.

acceptanceCriteria.text: .sdd/pipeline.md gains a `### `/inline-edit <ticket>`` section, placed between the `### `/re-gate ...`` section and `### `/hotfix ...``, defining the lane runtime-neutrally end to end: refuse/route -> planner (spec-first gate) -> the direct inline edit (no dev subagent) -> editor-authored changes.md/changes.json plus write-stamp.mjs -> tester -> review -> security -> `node scripts/ledger-append.mjs --inline --ticket <id> --why-inline "<reason>"`, naming red and dev as deliberately skipped rather than merely omitting them.

That section states the obligations checklist at five named stops (after planner/before any edit; after the edit; after tester; after review+security; after the ledger step), and each stop names what has been produced, which gates remain owed, which exact ledger command applies, and what gets recorded where.

That section states the abnormal-stop obligation explicitly: an abandoned inline lane writes no ledger entry and leaves an unrecorded hand-edit on disk (the D-005 #3 failure), and is discharged only by finishing the lane (plain, or composed with --override-review/--override-security for a non-PASS outcome) or by reverting the edit.

That section carries an "Honest limits" paragraph naming, at minimum: no red (tests written after the diff — the D-018 inversion, at any size, with no mechanical size bound and why lite's is deliberately not imported); no dev-stage isolation and self-reported changes.md; the "do not run /red here" rule being unenforced and why it cannot be detected at ledger time; and that --ticket plus the stamp check verify which ticket and shape, never that planner ran this round.

That section carries a "not this lane" routing table covering a production incident (/hotfix), re-verifying a run that already has a review.json (/re-gate), wanting an agent to implement it (/pipeline or /pipeline-lite), and a change where a spec-first test would earn its keep (/pipeline) — plus the recorded lite-vs-inline rule (D-3) in prose.
/inline-edit is named in .sdd/pipeline.md's opening paragraph and in its `## Entry points` preamble, not only inside its own section.

.claude/skills/inline-edit/SKILL.md exists, opens with YAML frontmatter carrying `name: inline-edit`, a non-empty description, `disable-model-invocation: true`, and a non-empty argument-hint; its body points at .sdd/pipeline.md as authoritative, restates only the easily-lost refusals, and stays under 60 lines.

.sdd/ledger/README.md gains an "Inline-edit entries" section documenting the exact entry.json shape (pinning the literals skippedStages, reason, note, size), the (INLINE) title marker and `## Inline edit` section, the condensed index.json `inline: { skippedStages }` decoration, the reason the entry is indexed rather than excluded, and the fact that it carries no red.json.

.sdd/stages/tester.md's Required inputs item 1 and its Output contract "Red suite result" bullet name the /inline-edit lane alongside /pipeline-lite as legitimate red.md-absent cases, with the D-018 guarantee unchanged; .sdd/stages/CHANGELOG.md gains a `## PL-12` entry naming tester.md as the only stage file amended; no other .sdd/stages/*.md file is modified.
/inline-edit is discoverable from CLAUDE.md's `## Agent pipeline` related-commands list, .sdd/README.md's directory-map pipeline.md line, and .sdd/README.md's `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` paragraph.

scripts/ledger-append.mjs --inline is a disclosure-only marker on the plain (non---hotfix) path that relaxes no gate: review.json and security.json must both still show PASS (or be accepted via --override-*), refuseIfStale still runs unconditionally on both, the unconditional spec.json/spec.md agreement check still runs, findCompletedSecurityRun still independently re-verifies the cited run against its own immutable manifest.json/results.json, and the run id is reused from that security run rather than minted.
--inline --lite and --inline --re-gate are each refused, with a distinct message naming why the lanes differ, before any .pipeline/ file is read.

--inline requires --ticket <id> (non-empty, not flag-shaped) and refuses unless extractTicketId(specJson.ticket) equals it; --ticket supplied with neither --re-gate nor --inline still fails, with the message widened to name both.

--inline requires --why-inline "<reason>", non-empty and not flag-shaped, and refuses without it ("no reason, no inline entry", the same posture --override-* takes); the reason is recorded verbatim in entry.json's inline.reason and rendered in entry.md's `## Inline edit` section.

--inline additionally requires .pipeline/spec.json to carry a stamp (presence and shape via readStamp, never freshness), and .pipeline/changes.md, .pipeline/changes.json, and .pipeline/test-results.md to exist — each with its own named refusal explaining why this lane requires it.

--inline never reads and never copies .pipeline/red.json; the entry's redTestPaths is [] and its redAbsenceNote is the fixed INLINE_RED_ABSENCE_NOTE, never the plain path's "predates / produced nothing" disjunction.

entry.json for a --inline run carries inline: { skippedStages: ["red","dev"], reason, note, size } with skippedStages and note derived from exported script constants and never caller-supplied (there is no --skipped-stages/--inline-note flag); the inline key is always present and is null on every other run.

entry.md for a --inline run is titled `# Ledger entry — <runId> (INLINE)` and carries a `## Inline edit` section immediately after `## Verdicts`, rendering note verbatim plus the skipped stages, the reason, and the measured size (or an explicit "could not be measured" statement); markers compose in the documented order (RE-GATE)(INLINE)(LITE)(OVERRIDE).

The change's size is measured via the already-imported countChangedLines/maxChangedLineLength for disclosure only — it never gates anything, and a measurement failure records size: null plus a printed note rather than refusing or silently omitting the field.

scripts/build-ledger-index.mjs reads entry.json's inline field strictly (fail-closed on a malformed one) and carries inline: { skippedStages } into every index.json record for that run's files, omitted entirely (not null) for every other run; the byte-for-byte { "review": "PASS", "security": "PASS" } verdicts gate is unchanged, and inline is not a widening case.

Coverage and wiring: [inline]-tagged cases exist in scripts/ledger-append.test.mjs, scripts/build-ledger-index.test.mjs, and scripts/sdd-completeness.test.mjs; no new script file is added, so package.json, .github/workflows/ci.yml, and scripts/tsconfig.json are unchanged; and .sdd/runtimes.yml, .sdd/bounds.yml, .claude/agents/**, and docs/PRD_Tickets.md are all untouched.

edgeCases.text: --inline with no --ticket: refuse, naming the flag and stating that it is the caller's own assertion, never derived from spec.json.
--inline --ticket X where extractTicketId(specJson.ticket) is Y: refuse, and say plainly that retrying with a fabricated --ticket is not the fix — ratify the correct spec first.

spec.json and spec.md disagree on the ticket: the existing unconditional agreement check fires first, on the inline path exactly as on every other; the --inline ticket check is not a replacement for it.
--inline with an unstamped spec.json: refuse, with the inline-specific clause in the message (no dev stage guarantees a freshly-written sidecar on this lane).
--inline with .pipeline/changes.md and/or changes.json missing: refuse, naming which one and why this lane requires it (there is no dev stage that would have written them).
--inline with .pipeline/test-results.md missing: refuse — tester is mandatory here.
--why-inline absent, empty, whitespace-only, or immediately followed by another --flag: refuse in every case, the same fail-closed shape readOverrideReason already uses.
--inline --lite and --inline --re-gate: each refused before any .pipeline/ read, with distinct messages.
A STALE review.json or security.json: refuseIfStale refuses, unchanged by this lane, and is not bypassable by --inline or by any override.

A non-PASS review.json or security.json: refuses without the matching --override-*; with it, the entry carries bypass: true, is excluded from index.json, and is titled (INLINE) (OVERRIDE) — the inline disclosure survives on the entry regardless, orthogonally, the same way regate and an override already compose.

A leftover .pipeline/red.json on disk: never read, never copied, never contributes to redTestPaths; no refusal, because a genuine same-round red.json is indistinguishable from a leftover at ledger time (its stamp is stale by construction on this lane) — stated as an honest limit rather than papered over with a check that cannot work.

The working tree is already clean at ledger time (the inline edit was committed first): filesTouched falls back to changes.json's filesChanged; a changes.json with an empty filesChanged against a clean tree still fails loudly, unchanged.

countChangedLines or maxChangedLineLength throws (git unavailable, an unresolvable ref, an unreadable file): measureInlineSize returns null, entry.json records "size": null, entry.md says so explicitly, a note is printed, and the write proceeds — measurement is disclosure, never a gate, so a failed measurement must not fail-closed into refusing a legitimate record.
The change includes a binary or otherwise unsizable file: its path is recorded in size.unsizable, so changedLines is never read as a complete count.

.sdd/ledger/<runId>/ already exists (a second append for the same security run): the existing overwrite guard refuses, reached on the inline path too; likewise copySecurityHistoryIntoLedger's own guard on an existing security/ directory.

build-ledger-index.mjs encounters an entry.json whose inline is malformed (not an object, skippedStages absent or not an array of strings): it fails closed, and --check fails loudly rather than reporting the index as up to date.

Back-compat: every ledger entry written before PL-12 carries no inline key at all; readInlineField must treat an absent key as null (never a validation failure), every existing entry.md/entry.json must be untouched, and `node scripts/build-ledger-index.mjs --check` must still pass against the pre-existing entries.

The lane is entered and abandoned after the edit but before the gates: nothing is recorded. The section must name this outcome and its two discharges (finish, or revert), because this is exactly the unrecorded hand-edit the lane exists to replace, and a lane that invites a human to edit is the one most likely to be walked away from.

review.json reads NEEDS_FIXES (or security.json BLOCKED) on this lane: route back to another inline edit (not /dev), re-run tester/review(/security), under the existing 3-attempt cap; red still never runs, and specifically must not be authored after the fix. At the cap: no ledger entry unless the outcome is recorded via --override-*.

The existing PL-11 assertions in scripts/sdd-completeness.test.mjs must keep passing: (a) the stage-file allowlist test permits only .sdd/stages/tester.md and .sdd/stages/CHANGELOG.md in `git diff --name-only HEAD -- .sdd/stages`, which PL-12 must not exceed; (b) pipelineLiteSection() slices between '### `/pipeline-lite' and '### Per-stage entry points', so the new section must be placed OUTSIDE that range (hence the /re-gate -> /hotfix placement) and a new inlineEditSection() helper anchored on '### `/inline-edit' ... '### `/hotfix' must be added rather than widening the existing one; (c) the [lite] tester.md assertions use 400-character coOccurs windows, so the inline-lane wording added to tester.md must not push 'lite' and 'red.md'/'state' further apart than that; (d) the generalized '### `/<command>`' to .claude/skills/<command>/SKILL.md test will automatically demand the new shim, and its commands.length >= 10 floor still holds.
